pairs.question: Abba, quæ fit, ut, cum ego in mea cellula faciam cuncta quæ decent, tamen non inveniam consolationem a Deo?
pairs.answer: Hoc tibi contingit eo, quod vanis cum otioso confabulationibus indulges; et quia omnino vis potiri optato voluntatem tuam propriam.
pairs.derivation: Direct exchange. Dropped speech tags 'interrogans senem dixit' and 'Ait illi senex'. Answer is the senex's full reply (two clauses giving the cause); stops before the next turn 'Reposuit seni'.

pairs.locus: Apophthegmata Macarii Magni 2 (Quid igitur facere me jubes)
pairs.question: Quid igitur facere me jubes, pater?
pairs.answer: Vade, ini familiaritatem cum viro timente Deum, et humilia te ipsum coram eo; et renuntia voluntati tuæ; et tunc invenies consolationem a Deo.
pairs.derivation: Second direct exchange in the same saying. Dropped tags 'Reposuit seni' and 'Respondit senex'. Answer is the complete imperative reply, which ends the saying.

pairs.question: Quid est, vivere hominem tanquam hospitem et peregrinum?
pairs.answer: Dic tibi: Tace, et non habeo hic negotium. Hæc itera et fac in omni loco et operatione; tunc eris vere in statu advenæ et peregrini.
pairs.derivation: Author frames the question 'Interrogatus est senex'. Dropped that tag and the inline speech tag 'inquit' (which split 'Dic, inquit, tibi'), giving 'Dic tibi'. Answer is the senex's whole reply explaining how to live as a stranger.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 2 (Macarius interrogat anachoretas)
pairs.question: Unde estis, et quomodo venistis in solitudinem hanc?
pairs.answer: E coenobio sumus atque ex mutuo consensu egressi venimus huc, ecce quadraginta abhinc anni præterierunt. Unus e nobis Aegyptius est, alter Libycus.
pairs.derivation: Direct exchange. Dropped tags 'Dixi illis' and 'Responderunt'. Answer is the hermits' complete reply (origin, how, when, who); stops before the narrative turn 'Ipsi quoque interrogaverunt me'.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 2 (Quanam ratione fieri potero monachus)
pairs.question: Quanam ratione fieri potero monachus?
pairs.answer: Nisi quis renuntiaverit omnibus mundi rebus, non potest fieri monachus.
pairs.derivation: Macarius asks how to become a monk. Dropped tags 'percontatus sum' and 'Aiunt mihi'. Answer is the hermits' single-sentence reply; stops before the next turn 'Excepi: Ego infirmus sum'.

pairs.question: Quo vadis?
pairs.answer: Proficiscor ad fratres, ut eis suggeram.
pairs.derivation: Macarius questions Satan on the road. Dropped tags 'Dicit ei magnus senex' and 'Respondit'. Answer is Satan's reply stating his destination and purpose; stops before the senex's next question 'Et quare tibi ampullæ hæ?'.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 3 (Quomodo vocatur frater ille)
pairs.question: Quomodo vocatur frater ille?
pairs.derivation: Macarius asks the demon the name of his one obedient 'friend'. Dropped tags 'Tum senex' and 'Satanas ad hoc'. Answer is the single name supplied; stops before 'Quo dicto discessit'.

pairs.question: Quomodo jejunas?
pairs.derivation: Macarius asks Theopemptus about his fasting. Dropped tags 'dicit ei' and 'Respondit'. Answer directly states the fasting hour; stops before the senex's instruction 'Jejuna usque ad vesperam'.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 11 (Quodnam est illud)
pairs.question: Quodnam est illud?
pairs.derivation: Self-contained with setup: the devil has just said 'Unum solum est in quo vincis me'. Macarius asks what that one thing is; dropped tag 'Interrogavit Abbas Macarius'. Answer 'Humilitas tua' directly names it; stops before 'Ac propterea adversus te nihil possum'.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 12 (Qui fit ut corpus siccum sit)
pairs.question: Qui fit, ut sive comedas, sive jejunes, corpus tuum pariter siccum sit?
pairs.answer: Lignum quod versat sarmenta quæ comburuntur, omnino ab igne consumitur. Simili modo si mentem suam homo in timore Dei mundaverit, ipse Dei timor corpus ejus consumit.
pairs.derivation: Some fathers ask why his body is dry whether he eats or fasts. Dropped tags 'dicentes' and 'Responditque illis senex'. Answer is the senex's full analogy-and-application reply, which ends the saying.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 15 (Quis te huc attulit)
pairs.question: Quis te huc attulit?
pairs.answer: Pater meus hic me projecit, et abiit.
pairs.derivation: Macarius questions the paralytic boy. Dropped tags 'interrogavit eum' and 'Respondit'. Answer states who brought him; stops before the senex's command 'Surgens assequere eum'.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 19 (Quomodo debemus orare)
pairs.question: Quomodo debemus orare?
pairs.answer: Non opus est loqui multum, sed extendendæ sunt manus, proferendumque: Domine, sicut vis et sicut nosti, miserere.
pairs.derivation: Some ask Macarius how to pray. Dropped tags 'dicentes' and 'Respondit ille senex'. Answer is the operative first sentence prescribing the manner of prayer; stops before the conditional elaboration 'Si autem ingruerit tentationis impugnatio'.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 24 (Quid hoc verbi est)
pairs.question: Quid hoc verbi est, pater, quod affectus sis admiratione?
pairs.answer: Revera Dominus noster dives est diligitque nos, nec volumus illi obtemperare; inimicus autem noster diabolus pauper est, odioque nos prosequitur, et diligimus ejus impuritatem.
pairs.derivation: The brothers ask why Macarius marvelled at the boy's words. Dropped tags 'Dicunt ei fratres' and 'Respondit illis senex'. Answer is the senex's full allegorical explanation, which ends the saying.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 27 (Quid est fugere homines)
pairs.question: Quid est fugere homines?
pairs.answer: Sedere in cella tua, et deflere tua peccata.
pairs.derivation: Abbas Esaias asks what fleeing men means (self-contained: the senex had just said 'Homines fuge'). Dropped tags 'Rursus Abbas Esaias' and 'Senex vero'. Normalized the source full stop to a question mark. Answer directly defines it; ends the saying.

pairs.locus: De Abbate Macario Aegyptio 38 (Tu quis es - calvaria)
pairs.question: Tu quis es?
pairs.answer: Ego eram pontifex idolorum, eorumque gentilium, qui hoc loco morabantur.
pairs.derivation: Macarius questions the speaking skull. Dropped tag 'Dico ei'; normalized source full stop to question mark. Answer is the skull's identifying first sentence; stops before it turns to address Macarius 'tu vero es Macarius'.
